title: 🏷️ Matching Headings — The Strategy

sections.heading: What this question type tests
sections.body:
You are given a list of headings (6–9 options) and must match each one to the correct paragraph. Typically only 5–7 paragraphs need headings (there are always more headings than paragraphs — the extras are distractors).

It tests: Can you identify the MAIN IDEA of a paragraph — not details.

sections.heading: The 4-step strategy
sections.body:
Step 1: Read ALL headings first — understand what each one means
Step 2: Read the FIRST and LAST sentence of the paragraph
Step 3: Match the heading that captures the paragraph's CENTRAL POINT
Step 4: Cross out used headings (one spare heading per question)

highlight: The most common mistake: matching a heading because one word appears in the paragraph. The heading must match the MAIN IDEA — not just mention the topic.

example.wrong: Paragraph mentions 'forests' once → matches heading 'Forest conservation efforts'
example.right: The paragraph is MAINLY about deforestation causes → matches heading 'Factors driving forest loss'

title: ⚠️ The Three Heading Traps
body:
TRAP 1 — Detail not main idea:
A word from the heading appears once in the paragraph but isn't the main focus.

TRAP 2 — Too specific:
The heading describes one example from the paragraph, but the paragraph covers a broader topic.

TRAP 3 — Similar headings:
Two headings look similar — one is for THIS paragraph, one is for another. Always check both paragraphs before deciding.

Test: Remove the heading from your mind and summarise the paragraph in 4 words. Does the heading match your summary?

quick.label: Ask: what is this paragraph MAINLY about?

question: A paragraph discusses several examples of government policies that failed to reduce pollution. Which heading fits BEST?
options: The causes of air pollution in cities
Why environmental legislation has proven ineffective
The role of governments in addressing climate change
How businesses respond to pollution regulations
correct: Why environmental legislation has proven ineffective
explanation:
The paragraph is MAINLY about government policies that FAILED — so the heading must capture that failure.

✅ 'Why environmental legislation has proven ineffective' = matches main idea (legislation + ineffective)

❌ 'The causes of air pollution' = too broad; the paragraph is specifically about policy failure
❌ 'The role of governments in addressing climate change' = too general; doesn't capture the failure angle
❌ 'How businesses respond' = businesses aren't mentioned
hint: The heading must match what the paragraph is MAINLY arguing — not just its topic.

question: You have narrowed it down to two headings for one paragraph. What is the best next step?
options: Choose the longer heading — it has more detail
Choose the first heading that occurred to you
Read the paragraph again focusing on the first and last sentences, then compare both headings
Leave it blank and come back later
correct: Read the paragraph again focusing on the first and last sentences, then compare both headings
explanation:
When two headings both seem possible:
1. Reread the first sentence — usually the topic sentence (main idea)
2. Reread the last sentence — usually the conclusion or main point
3. Ask: which heading matches the OVERALL paragraph, not just one part?

Often, one heading describes a detail from the middle of the paragraph. The correct heading covers the WHOLE paragraph's point.
hint: The topic sentence (first sentence) and concluding sentence usually reveal the main idea.

question: Paragraph text: 'While solar energy has grown rapidly, the infrastructure required for large-scale adoption remains costly. Battery storage technology, though improving, cannot yet support national grids. Furthermore, political resistance in fossil-fuel-dependent economies creates additional barriers.' Best heading?
options: The benefits of solar energy for the environment
Why solar energy adoption faces multiple barriers
Political opposition to renewable energy sources
correct: Why solar energy adoption faces multiple barriers
explanation:
The paragraph lists THREE different barriers:
1. Costly infrastructure
2. Battery storage limitations
3. Political resistance

The heading must capture ALL THREE — which means the overall theme is 'multiple barriers to solar adoption.'

❌ 'Battery storage technology' = only covers one of three points
❌ 'Political opposition' = only covers one of three points
❌ 'Benefits of solar energy' = the paragraph is about PROBLEMS, not benefits
hint: Count how many different ideas the paragraph contains — the heading should cover all of them.

question: In matching headings, what should you do with headings you have already used?
options: Keep considering them for other paragraphs
Cross them out — each heading is used only once
They can be used twice if they fit
Save them for the hardest paragraphs
correct: Cross them out — each heading is used only once
explanation:
Each heading is used ONCE ONLY in matching headings questions.

Crossing out used headings:
✅ Reduces your options for remaining paragraphs
✅ Makes the process faster
✅ Prevents accidentally reusing the same heading

Note: There will always be MORE headings than paragraphs — 2–3 headings will be unused. Don't be surprised by this.
hint: More headings than paragraphs is by design — the extras are distractors.
